s3268: A person entitled to drive both category "C" and category "D" vehicles may carry more than eight passengers in the cargo body of a truck fitted out in the prescribed manner no sooner than how long after obtaining a category "C" driving licence?
s3269: According to subparagraph "b" of paragraph 3 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, if there are more than 8 passengers, passengers may be carried in the cargo body of a truck only by a person who meets the requirements of paragraph 8 of Article 56 of this Law. According to paragraph 8 of Article 56 of the same Law, a person entitled to drive category "C" and "D" vehicles may, 3 years after obtaining a category "C" driving licence, carry more than 8 passengers in the cargo body of a truck fitted out in the manner prescribed by the legislation of Georgia.
s3272: The number of passengers carried in the fitted-out cargo body of a truck:
s3270: Must not exceed the number of seats provided
s3273: According to paragraph 5 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the number of passengers carried in the cargo body of a truck must not exceed the number of seats provided. Before setting off, the truck driver must brief the passengers on how to board and where to sit in the cargo body. The driver may start moving only after making sure that all the conditions for carrying the passengers safely are met.
s3277: If the vehicle has seats placed below the level of its sides, who may ride in the cargo body of a truck that is not fitted out for passengers?
s3274: Only a person accompanying or receiving the cargo
s3276: Any adult, except elderly people and pregnant women
s3278: According to paragraph 6 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, only a person accompanying or receiving the cargo may ride in the cargo body of a flatbed truck that is not fitted out for carrying passengers, and only if the vehicle has seats placed below the level of its sides.
s3283: When a group of children is carried in a flatbed truck fitted out for carrying passengers, the height of the sides from the floor must not be:
s3281: Less than 0.3 metres or more than 0.5 metres
s3282: Less than 0.4 metres or more than 0.7 metres
s3284: According to paragraph 9 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, a flatbed truck used for carrying passengers must have seats placed 0.3–0.5 metres above the floor and at least 0.3 metres below the top edge of the sides, and when a group of children is carried, the height of the sides from the floor must not be less than 0.8 metres. Seats placed along the rear or side panels must have rigid backrests.
s3286: Carrying passengers in the fitted-out cargo body of a truck is permitted:
s3287: According to subparagraph "c" of paragraph 2 of Article 23 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when travelling in a flatbed truck, a passenger is prohibited from standing in the cargo body, sitting on the sides or placing cargo on them.
s3291: When a group of children is carried in the fitted-out cargo body of a truck, they must be accompanied by at least:
s3292: According to paragraph 7 of Article 46 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, when a group of children is carried by bus or in a van-bodied truck, the group must be accompanied by an adult escort, and when it is carried in the cargo body of a flatbed truck fitted with seats, by at least two such persons. The identification sign "Transporting children" must be fixed to the front and rear of the vehicle.
s3296: In what order must the vehicles go through the intersection when moving in the direction of the arrows, if the emergency service vehicle has its flashing blue special light switched on?

s3295: First the emergency service vehicle, then the bus, and finally the tram
s3297: According to subparagraphs "a" and "c" of paragraph 4 of Article 36 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, at an uncontrolled intersection: a) where roads of unequal importance cross, the driver of a vehicle on the secondary road must give way to vehicles approaching on the main road, regardless of the direction in which they will continue; c) where roads of equal importance cross, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles approaching from the right. Drivers of rail vehicles must follow the same rule among themselves. At such an intersection, a rail vehicle has priority over trackless vehicles, regardless of its direction of travel. According to paragraph 1 of Article 51 of the same Law, the driver of an emergency or special service vehicle who has the flashing blue special light switched on and is carrying out an official duty may depart from the requirements of Articles 25, 31−41 and 44 of this Law and of Annexes No. 1 and No. 2 to this Law, provided that road safety is ensured. A flashing red light may also be switched on in addition to the flashing blue special light. To obtain priority over other road users, the driver of such a vehicle must switch on both the flashing blue special light and the siren.
s3299: Which car's driver must give way when moving in the direction of the arrow, if the ambulance does not have its flashing blue special light switched on?
s3300: According to paragraph 1 of Article 51 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver of an emergency or special service vehicle who has the flashing blue special light switched on and is carrying out an official duty may depart from the requirements of Articles 25, 31−41 and 44 of this Law and of Annexes No. 1 and No. 2 to this Law, provided that road safety is ensured. A flashing red light may also be switched on in addition to the flashing blue special light. To obtain priority over other road users, the driver of such a vehicle must switch on both the flashing blue special light and the siren. According to subparagraph "c" of paragraph 4 of Article 36 of the same Law, at an uncontrolled intersection where roads of equal importance cross, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles approaching from the right.

s3371: Which of the following can cause a rear-end collision with a vehicle?
s3368: Only failing to keep a proper distance to the vehicle ahead
s3370: Only sudden, sharp braking by the vehicle ahead
s3372: According to paragraph 11 of Article 33 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver of a vehicle following another vehicle must keep a proper distance, so as to avoid a collision if the vehicle ahead brakes or stops suddenly. Keeping a proper side interval is also necessary for road safety. According to subparagraph "l" of paragraph 10 of Article 25 of the same Law, when overtaking, dangerous situations most often arise from not keeping a safe distance and from paying too little attention to vehicles travelling in the opposite direction.

s3389: Brake sharply until the car comes to a complete stop

s3393: Only the driver of the red car

According to subparagraph "d" of paragraph 6 of Article 45 of the same Law, towing with a motorcycle without a sidecar, and towing such a motorcycle, is prohibited.

s3397: Only the drivers of the towing and the towed motorcycle

Overtaking a vehicle that is overtaking or going around an obstacle is prohibited. s3416: In this situation, how many requirements of the rules of the road are being broken, if the vehicles towed with a flexible coupling are travelling at 50 km/h and the distance between them is 5 metres?
s3417: According to paragraphs 7, 8 and 9 of Article 45 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic: 7. At any time of day, the towing motor vehicle must have its dipped-beam headlights switched on, and the towed motor vehicle must have its hazard warning lights switched on; if it has none, or they are faulty, a warning triangle must be fixed to the rear of the towed vehicle. 8. When a motor vehicle is being towed, the towing (coupling) device must be marked with flags or another warning device, so that other road users can easily notice it at any time of day. 9. When a motor vehicle is being towed, flexible coupling links are marked with flags, a warning device, or a 200×200 mm plate with alternating red and white diagonal stripes 50 mm wide and a reflective surface. At least two warning devices (flags) are fixed to a flexible coupling link. According to paragraph 11 of Article 31 of the same Law, outside built-up areas, and in built-up areas on sections of the carriageway where driving at more than 80 km/h is allowed, the driver must keep as close as possible to the right-hand edge of the carriageway. Occupying the left lane when the right lane is free is prohibited, except when going around an obstacle, turning left or making a U-turn. The violations here are: the position on the carriageway; the towing car does not have its dipped-beam headlights switched on; the towed car does not have its hazard warning lights switched on; and the towing device is not marked with flags.
s3419: According to paragraph 7.2 of Chapter 7 (Information signs) of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, road sign 7.2 "Recommended speed" shows the speed at which it is recommended to drive on the given section of road. s3421: In this situation, is the driver of the towing car prohibited from moving in the direction of the arrow if the road is icy?

s3445: Is it prohibited to tow a motor vehicle that has two trailers?
s3446: According to subparagraph "b" of paragraph 6 of Article 45 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, towing two or more motor vehicles, and towing a motor vehicle that has two or more trailers, is prohibited.

s3474: In this situation, how many rules of the road is the driver of the towing truck moving in the direction of the arrow breaking, if it is travelling at 60 km/h?
